e.440128614:
A water softener is a household water treatment system that removes the minerals responsible for hard water, mainly calcium and magnesium.
Hard water is common in many homes. Although it is generally safe to drink, it can cause mineral buildup in plumbing, appliances, showers, and faucets.
A water softener helps reduce these problems by making the water softer.

 1. Softer skin and hair – Reduces mineral residue that can leave skin feeling dry and hair feeling dull or stiff.
2. Cleaner dishes and glassware – Helps prevent white spots, cloudy glasses, and mineral deposits.
3. Less soap and detergent – Soap lathers better in soft water, so you may use less laundry detergent, shampoo, and dish soap.
4. Longer appliance lifespan – Helps prevent scale buildup in dishwashers, washing machines, water heaters, and other water-using appliances.
5. Improved water heater efficiency – Reduces mineral buildup that can make water heaters work harder and use more energy.
6. Cleaner plumbing pipes – Helps prevent calcium and magnesium scale from accumulating inside pipes.
7. Softer, brighter laundry – Clothes can feel less stiff and may retain their color and softness better.
8. Less cleaning around the house – Reduces hard-water spots and crusty buildup on faucets, showerheads, tubs, and sinks.
9. Better shower experience – Helps soap and shampoo rinse away more easily.
10. Potential long-term savings – Less scale buildup can mean fewer appliance repairs, less cleaning, and reduced soap usage.

Verified all connections are tight and make sure all breaker sizes are within spec of the conductor ethic control. One major thing I didn’t notice is that there is a good amount of corrosion forming on the main neutral lug, as well as a little bit on the ground and neutral bar. I was informed that a lot of water and moisture tends to sleep through the walls in the basement which could be a possibility of where this is coming from. I also noticed that the exterior service is over 30 years old, which that could be the cause behind that as well. I did open up the meter base and only noticed little corrosion. However, the service wire goes under a roof for the balcony which is not convenient or up to code due to personnel being able to grab a hold of the conductor with the connections. Inform the homeowner that we are not 100% positive of where that corrosion for the panel is coming from but due to the age and location of the exterior service, I recommended replacing it with a service mast riser, which will go straight up from the meter base through the roof.. Power company will need to be contacted to run a new line from our service mast to the transformer. Inform the homeowner that replacing the service does not guarantee a fix to the corrosion but it is definitely highly recommended to replace. The only other thing I noticed during today’s evaluation is that the gas and water system is not properly bonded/grounded. A number for copper wire is required to go from the main electrical panel to the water meter, as well as the gas manifold to protect people from any shriveled shock on any gas, appliance or water fixture. I provide a option to replace the service which includes the grounding and bonding as well as a separate option for the grounding and bonding. All other electrical components are at the home or up to code and tested properly today. Emailed invoices and estimates to the homeowner.I completed the annual electrical system evaluation, beginning at the main electrical panel. Voltage readings were within acceptable ranges, all electrical connections were checked for proper tightness, and breaker sizes were verified to ensure they were appropriately rated for the connected conductors.

During the inspection, I discovered a noticeable amount of corrosion forming on the main neutral lug, along with minor corrosion on the neutral and grounding bars. Although the electrical system is currently operating and voltage readings are acceptable, continued corrosion can eventually compromise electrical connections and potentially lead to intermittent power loss, flickering lights, and other electrical distribution issues.

The exact source of the corrosion could not be determined during today’s evaluation. The homeowner mentioned that water and moisture have historically seeped through the basement walls, which could potentially contribute to the issue. Additionally, the exterior electrical service is over 30 years old, and its age and existing installation conditions may also be contributing factors.

I inspected the meter base and observed only minor corrosion in that location. However, I also identified concerns with the existing exterior service installation. The service conductors currently run underneath the balcony roof, leaving portions of the wiring and connections accessible to individuals. This installation is not ideal from a safety and code-compliance standpoint.

Due to the age and configuration of the existing exterior service, I highly recommend replacing it with a new service mast and riser. The proposed installation would extend vertically from the meter base, through the roof, providing a more appropriate and protected route for the service conductors. The utility company will also need to be contacted to coordinate running a new service line from the transformer to the newly installed service mast.

Important: Replacing the exterior electrical service does not guarantee that the corrosion currently present inside the main electrical panel will be eliminated. We cannot confirm the exact source of the corrosion at this time. However, given the age and condition of the existing service, replacement is strongly recommended as a preventative safety measure and to address the concerns with the current installation.

Another issue identified during today’s evaluation involves the home’s grounding and bonding system. The existing gas and water systems are not properly bonded to the electrical grounding system. Proper bonding conductors need to be installed from the main electrical panel to the water service piping and gas manifold. This bonding is essential to help prevent dangerous voltage differences and reduce the risk of electrical shock when touching plumbing fixtures or gas appliances.

I provided the homeowner with two separate options:

1. Complete Service Replacement: Includes replacement of the exterior electrical service with a new service mast and riser, along with the necessary grounding and bonding improvements.
2. Grounding and Bonding Only: Addresses the deficiencies in the existing grounding and bonding system without replacing the exterior electrical service.

All other electrical components evaluated throughout the home were found to be operating properly and were tested within acceptable parameters at the time of today’s inspection.

Invoices and estimates outlining the recommended work and available options were emailed to the homeowner for review and consideration.

Lastly, we identified two junction boxes that do not have the any covers installed and two sets of open splices that have been taped for the lighting above the workshop area. Overall, we found very few areas of concern. The existing electrical panel is older, but upon inspection, all breaker connections were tight and secure, with no immediate concerns identified. The homeowner has done a great job maintaining the home’s electrical devices and keeping up with replacements. The receptacles, switches, and other devices inspected throughout the areas we accessed were generally in great condition.

During our evaluation, LPH discussed a few opportunities to improve the home’s electrical safety and protection, including:

* Installing GFCI protection for the garbage disposal to provide additional protection against electrical shock around a water-connected appliance.
* Addressing the garage receptacle that is currently missing GFCI protection.
* Replacing one living room receptacle that is beginning to crack to prevent further deterioration and maintain a safe, reliable connection.
* Providing an estimate to install a grounding connection at the incoming water meter. This supplements the home’s existing ground rods as part of the grounding and bonding system, helping provide a proper path for electrical fault current and meeting applicable code requirements.
* Providing an estimate to replace the existing covered patio receptacle with a 20-amp tamper-resistant, weather-resistant GFCI. Although the existing receptacle is already GFCI protected, it is not weather-rated. Upgrading it will provide better resistance to moisture and corrosion, helping prevent deteriorating contacts, poor electrical connections, overheating, and premature receptacle failure.

We reviewed all findings and recommendations with the homeowner. We also discussed that the homeowner is very capable of replacing electrical devices independently and has done an excellent job maintaining the home. The additional estimates for the water meter grounding and weather-resistant patio receptacle were provided for convenience so the homeowner can review these improvements and determine what works best moving forward.

Overall, the electrical components inspected were in good condition, with only a handful of recommendations to consider. All estimates and today’s electrical system check evaluation and invoice summary will be emailed to the homeowner for review.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure speaking with you, and we look forward to servicing you again in the future!

e.440794236:
LPH will replace the existing patio receptacle with a new 20-amp tamper-resistant, weather-resistant GFCI receptacle.

The existing receptacle is already GFCI protected, but it is not weather-rated for outdoor conditions. Even under a covered patio, humidity, moisture, and temperature changes can affect standard receptacles over time. These conditions can cause internal contacts and connection points to corrode or rust, leading to poor electrical connections, increased resistance, overheating, intermittent power, and eventual receptacle failure.

Upgrading to a properly weather-rated GFCI provides the same ground-fault protection while adding the durability needed for outdoor environments. The weather-resistant construction is designed to better withstand moisture and corrosion, helping maintain a reliable electrical connection and reduce the likelihood of premature deterioration.

This upgrade provides an additional layer of protection and helps ensure the outdoor receptacle is properly suited for its environment.
e.440819632:
LPH will install a grounding connection to the incoming water service at the home’s water meter. This connection is an important part of the home’s electrical grounding and bonding system and works alongside the existing ground rods to provide the proper grounding protection.

In the event of an electrical fault, the grounding and bonding system provides a low-impedance path for fault current to return to its source, helping the breaker trip and disconnect power to the affected circuit. Bonding the incoming metallic water service also helps keep conductive components at the same electrical potential, reducing the risk of electrical shock.

Even if the majority of the home’s plumbing has been converted to plastic, the incoming water service and any remaining metallic piping still need to be properly evaluated and bonded. The water service connection serves as a supplementary grounding connection alongside the home’s ground rods, where required by the applicable electrical code.

LPH will install the appropriate grounding conductor and secure the connection at the water meter to help ensure the home’s grounding and bonding system is properly established and operating as intended.

A whole home surge protection device that gets mounted and connected at the panel will help defend against these harmful spikes of voltage. The device installed will come with lifetime parts warranty and up to $100,000 of repair or replacement (whichever is less) of coverage in the event that a grounded appliance or piece of equipment that are commonly found within a home such as A/C, Furnace, other home intergraded heating system (boilers and water heaters), water purification system, range, microwave, refrigerator, and etc.) becomes damaged due to a surge with this device installed. *Whole home surge protection device is NOT a power conditioner, meaning that the home surge device will not eliminate the minor flickering for bulbs entirely but will alleviate most of the major/noticeable flickering/strobing*. With windows and doors remaining closed more frequently and heating systems running regularly, airborne particles and other contaminants can circulate throughout your home.

LPH recommends considering the following indoor air quality upgrades to help improve air filtration, reduce certain airborne contaminants, and support a cleaner, healthier indoor environment.

1. UV Air Purification Light

A UV air purification light is installed within your home’s HVAC system and uses ultraviolet light technology to help reduce certain airborne microorganisms as air circulates through the system. This technology can help support improved indoor air quality and provide an additional layer of protection against certain biological contaminants.

2. Electric Air Cleaner with Upgraded Filtration

An electric air cleaner with upgraded filtration is designed to capture airborne particles, including dust, pollen, and other common indoor particulates. By enhancing your HVAC system’s filtration capabilities, this upgrade can help improve indoor air quality, reduce particle circulation, and keep internal HVAC components cleaner.

Why Consider These Upgrades?

During the heating season, your HVAC system plays an important role in circulating and filtering the air throughout your home. Improving your system’s air purification and filtration capabilities can provide several benefits:

* Help reduce certain airborne contaminants and microorganisms.
* Capture more airborne particles, including dust and pollen.
* Support cleaner air circulation throughout your home.
* Help keep HVAC system components cleaner.
* Improve overall indoor comfort and air quality.

Prepare Your Home for the Winter Season

LPH encourages homeowners to explore these indoor air quality solutions before the heating season gets underway. Investing in enhanced air purification and filtration can be a proactive step toward maintaining a cleaner and more comfortable home environment throughout the winter months.

For more information about these upgrades and to determine which option may be best suited for your home’s HVAC system, contact LPH. We’re happy to help you make an informed decision about your indoor air quality needs.

A spin-down sediment filter is designed to capture larger particles such as sand, silt, rust, and debris before they enter the home’s plumbing system. Unlike disposable cartridge filters, a spin-down filter uses a reusable stainless steel mesh screen that can be flushed clean by opening a purge valve, making maintenance quick and cost-effective.

The filter is typically installed on the main water line immediately after the water service enters the home and before other water treatment equipment, such as a water softener, iron filter, UV system, or water heater. Installing a spin-down filter helps protect plumbing fixtures and appliances from sediment buildup, extends the life of downstream filtration equipment, and reduces maintenance on water treatment systems.

The filter should be mounted where there is adequate clearance for servicing, and a drain or bucket should be available for periodic flushing. Routine maintenance involves opening the flush valve for several seconds to remove accumulated sediment, helping ensure reliable water flow and continued protection of the home’s plumbing system.

The existing well pump system is not equipped with a constant pressure switch. Due to the size of the home and the potential demand on the well system, the technician recommends installing a constant pressure switch to help maintain consistent water pressure throughout the home. This system would regulate the well pump to maintain a target pressure of approximately 60 PSI, helping provide more consistent water pressure when multiple plumbing fixtures are in use. Maintaining stable operating pressure can also help reduce unnecessary cycling of the well pump, potentially extending the life of the pump and improving the overall performance of the well system.

The spin-down filter will help capture larger particles and debris before the water reaches the 20-inch sediment filter, allowing the finer filter to capture smaller sediment particles. This two-stage filtration setup will help reduce sediment entering the home’s plumbing system, protect plumbing fixtures and water-using appliances, and improve overall water quality.

A spin down sediment filter is designed to capture larger particles such as sand, silt, rust, and debris before they enter the home’s plumbing system. Unlike disposable cartridge filters, a spin-down filter uses a reusable stainless steel mesh screen that can be flushed clean by opening a purge valve, making maintenance quick and cost-effective.

The filter is typically installed on the main water line immediately after the water service enters the home and before other water treatment equipment, such as a water softener, iron filter, UV system, or water heater. Installing a spin-down filter helps protect plumbing fixtures and appliances from sediment buildup, extends the life of downstream filtration equipment, and reduces maintenance on water treatment systems.

The filter should be mounted where there is adequate clearance for servicing, and a drain or bucket should be available for periodic flushing. Routine maintenance involves opening the flush valve for several seconds to remove accumulated sediment, helping ensure reliable water flow and continued protection of the home’s plumbing system.

i.334154566:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, Janet mentioned an issue with her baseboard thermostat in the second floor. Bathroom would not function at all, and the display was completely blank. During our thorough evaluation, we identified that the existing baseboard thermostat failed internally and needed to be replaced.

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, most of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, there are a few recommendations we assessed during this inspection. 

First we discovered that there are multiple locations where more than one wire is landed under one breaker termination screw, which increases the chance of loose  connections. Second we noticed that this electrical system is currently within the “end of life” range, which means the longevity is in question. This main electrical/distribution panel is also maxed out and most newer circuit or electrical equipment could not be installed within this existing panel. Lastly, there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. The immediate electrical package was approved by Janet and completed today. We installed a new Mysa smart baseboard thermostat that was tested, paired to the homeowner smart phone, and working properly prior to leaving today. We will honor a one year worry free parts and labor warranty for the new baseboard thermostat that was installed today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

LPH arrived at the home to perform an electrical system check and evaluate the condition of the home’s existing electrical service and electrical components.

During today’s evaluation, we identified deterioration affecting several components of the existing 100 Amp overhead electrical service. The existing meter base is not properly sealed, compromising its ability to prevent moisture from entering the electrical enclosure. Moisture intrusion can contribute to corrosion at electrical connection points and accelerate deterioration of the service equipment.

We also observed yellow discoloration on the insulation of the incoming overhead service cable. This discoloration is consistent with deterioration and contamination associated with aluminum oxide, a byproduct of corrosion on aluminum conductors. This raises concerns about the condition and long-term reliability of the incoming service conductors and their connections.

Based on the age and condition of the existing service equipment, LPH recommends addressing these concerns rather than allowing the deterioration to continue. We reviewed several different options with the homeowner so she could consider the level of replacement and improvements that best fit her needs.

Service Replacement Options Reviewed

1. Complete 200 Amp Overhead Electrical Service Upgrade

We presented the option of replacing the existing 100 Amp service with a complete 200 Amp overhead electrical service. This is the most comprehensive option and would include:

* New 200 Amp meter base and properly sized overhead service entrance cable.
* New service head/weatherhead and associated overhead service components.
* Properly secured and sealed exterior service connections.
* Protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections.
* New 200 Amp exterior emergency disconnect.
* New 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel and appropriately sized breakers.
* Whole-home surge protection.
* Complete grounding and bonding improvements, including two grounding electrodes and the appropriate connections.
* Required permits, inspections, and PPL coordination.

We discussed the benefits of increasing the home’s electrical capacity from 100 Amps to 200 Amps. This would provide additional capacity and flexibility for future HVAC equipment, electric vehicle charging, appliance upgrades, home renovations, and other electrical improvements. Completing the upgrade now would also allow the homeowner to address the existing service deterioration while investing in additional capacity for future needs.

2. Complete 100 Amp Overhead Electrical Service Replacement

We also reviewed the option of replacing the existing overhead electrical service while maintaining the home’s current 100 Amp capacity.

This option would address the deteriorated exterior service components without increasing the home’s electrical capacity to 200 Amps. The scope would include replacement of the meter base, overhead service entrance cable, service head/weatherhead, and installation of a new 100 Amp exterior emergency disconnect, along with the necessary service connections, sealing, permits, inspections, and utility coordination.

This option would address the existing exterior service concerns while keeping the home at its current 100 Amp service rating.

3. Exterior-Only 100 Amp Service Replacement

A separate option was also provided to replace only the exterior components of the existing 100 Amp overhead service.

This estimate focuses on:

* New 100 Amp meter base.
* New overhead service entrance cable.
* New service head/weatherhead.
* Properly secured and sealed exterior service components.
* Protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections.
* New 100 Amp exterior emergency disconnect.
* Required permits, inspections, and PPL coordination.

This option would address the deterioration identified on the exterior service equipment without including replacement of the interior electrical panel or additional grounding and bonding improvements.

4. Grounding and Bonding Improvements

We also provided a separate estimate to install the home’s grounding and bonding components. This option includes:

* Installation of two new grounding rods.
* Installation of properly sized grounding electrode conductors.
* Proper bonding of the home’s gas piping system.
* Proper grounding and bonding connections for the home’s water piping.
* Verification of the completed grounding and bonding connections.

This work would help establish the proper grounding and bonding system for the home and provide an appropriate path for electrical fault current.

Additional Electrical Findings

Aside from the primary service-related concerns, we identified a few smaller electrical items during today’s system check:

* The kitchen is lacking GFCI protection at the locations where it is required.
* An existing basement GFCI receptacle is no longer functioning as intended and should be replaced.
* Several receptacles are loose and are no longer maintaining proper connections with plugs inserted into them.

Although these items should be addressed, we did not include them in today’s estimates. We wanted to keep the primary focus on the more pressing concerns involving the existing electrical service and the available replacement and grounding options. These smaller items can be addressed separately.

Customer Discussion & Next Steps

LPH reviewed all of the findings and discussed the different estimates and available options with the homeowner. We went over the benefits of a complete 200 Amp service upgrade, replacing the existing service while maintaining 100 Amp capacity, replacing only the exterior 100 Amp service components, and completing the home’s grounding and bonding improvements.

At this time, the homeowner would like some time to review everything and consider the different options before making a decision on how she would like to proceed. No work was approved for scheduling during today’s visit.

LPH will email today’s electrical system check evaluation along with all of the service replacement and grounding estimates so the homeowner can take her time reviewing everything.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home and giving us the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system. It was a pleasure speaking with you, and we appreciate the opportunity to provide these options. We look forward to assisting you whenever you are ready to move forward.

e.440861937:
Complete 200 Amp Overhead Electrical Service Upgrade

Electrical Service Concerns

During the electrical system evaluation, LPH identified deterioration affecting several components of the home’s existing 100 Amp overhead electrical service.

The existing meter base was not properly sealed, compromising its ability to prevent moisture from entering the electrical enclosure. Moisture intrusion can contribute to corrosion at electrical connection points and accelerate deterioration of the service equipment.

LPH also observed yellow discoloration on the insulation of the overhead service cable entering the home. This discoloration is consistent with deterioration and contamination associated with aluminum oxide, a byproduct of corrosion on aluminum conductors. This condition raises concerns about the integrity of the incoming service conductors, particularly the neutral conductor and its connections. As corrosion progresses, electrical connections can experience increased resistance, overheating, and reduced reliability.

Due to the age and condition of the existing service components, improperly sealed meter base, and signs of deterioration on the incoming service cable, LPH recommends replacing the existing electrical service.

While the home currently operates on a 100 Amp service, LPH also recommends considering an upgrade to 200 Amp capacity while completing this replacement project. Since the meter base, overhead service cable, emergency disconnect, interior panel, and grounding system will already need to be replaced, this presents an ideal opportunity to increase the home’s electrical capacity without having to revisit much of this same work in the future.

Why Upgrade to 200 Amps?

A 100 Amp electrical service may adequately support the home’s existing electrical demands, but modern homes often require more electrical capacity as appliances, technology, and additional equipment are introduced.

Upgrading to 200 Amps provides significantly more available electrical capacity and gives the homeowner greater flexibility for future improvements.

Some benefits include:

* Future HVAC Upgrades: Additional capacity for larger heating and cooling equipment, heat pumps, and other electrical mechanical systems.
* Electric Vehicle Charging: Better preparation for installing a Level 2 EV charging station without as much concern about available service capacity.
* Kitchen and Appliance Upgrades: More capacity for additional or upgraded appliances, electric ranges, ovens, dryers, and other household equipment.
* Home Additions and Renovations: Greater flexibility when adding rooms, finishing a basement, or completing other electrical improvements.
* Future Electrification: Better preparation for transitioning to additional electric appliances and equipment.
* Additional Panel Capacity: A new 42-space panel provides room for additional circuits and future electrical needs.

Most importantly, upgrading now allows the homeowner to address the existing deterioration while investing in a service that is better prepared for future electrical demands.

Rather than replacing the existing equipment with another 100 Amp service and potentially paying for another service upgrade down the road, increasing to 200 Amps now allows the homeowner to complete the project once and establish a stronger foundation for future improvements.

Scope of Work Includes

1. Complete 200 Amp Overhead Electrical Service Replacement

* Remove and replace the existing meter base with a new 200 Amp meter base.
* Remove and replace the existing overhead service entrance cable with new properly sized 200 Amp service conductors.
* Install a new service head and weatherhead assembly.
* Replace associated overhead service components as required.
* Properly secure and support the new overhead service cable.
* Properly seal the meter base and associated entry points to help prevent future moisture intrusion.
* Install protective conduit over applicable exterior service cable sections to protect against sunlight exposure, physical damage, and premature insulation deterioration.
* Properly terminate, secure, and torque all service connections in accordance with manufacturer specifications and applicable electrical requirements.

2. New 200 Amp Exterior Emergency Disconnect

* Install a new 200 Amp exterior emergency service disconnect.
* Properly connect and configure the disconnect as part of the new electrical service.
* Install required identification and labeling.
* Verify proper operation as part of the completed installation.

The exterior emergency disconnect provides an accessible means of shutting off electrical power to the home during an emergency or when electrical service work is required. This improves accessibility for emergency responders and electrical service personnel while bringing the service configuration up to applicable electrical code requirements.

3. Interior Electrical Panel Replacement

* Remove the existing electrical panel.
* Install a new 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel rated for the upgraded 200 Amp service.
* Transfer and properly terminate the existing branch circuit wiring where conductors are suitable for reuse.
* Inspect accessible branch circuit conductors and connections for signs of water damage, corrosion, overheating, or deterioration.
* Install appropriately sized breakers for the existing circuits.
* Properly configure neutral and grounding connections as required at the new service equipment.
* Properly label the new electrical panel and identify the branch circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation.

The new 42-space Eaton CH panel will provide additional breaker capacity and room for future circuits, helping accommodate the homeowner’s electrical needs as the home evolves.

4. Whole-Home Surge Protection

* Install a whole-home surge protective device at the new electrical panel.
* Properly integrate the device into the electrical system.
* Verify proper installation and operation.

Whole-home surge protection helps protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other connected equipment against damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and electrical events originating within the home.

Everyday electrical equipment such as air conditioning systems, refrigerators, washers, dryers, dishwashers, and other appliances can create small internal voltage fluctuations. Larger surges can also enter through the utility supply during lightning activity or utility disturbances. Whole-home surge protection provides an additional layer of defense against these events.

5. Complete Grounding and Bonding Upgrade

* Install a complete grounding electrode system for the home.
* Install two grounding electrodes where permitted and required by applicable electrical codes.
* Connect the grounding electrodes using properly sized grounding electrode conductors.
* Establish and properly bond the qualifying metal water piping grounding connection.
* Verify that the water piping connection is continuous and suitable for use as part of the grounding and bonding system.
* Properly configure grounding and bonding connections at the new service equipment.
* Verify the completed grounding and bonding system.

A properly installed grounding and bonding system provides an essential path for electrical fault current and helps protective devices operate as intended during electrical faults. This is an important part of bringing the home’s electrical service up to modern safety standards.

6. Permits, Inspections, and Utility Coordination

* Coordinate with PPL for the 200 Amp overhead service upgrade.
* Obtain all necessary permits.
* Coordinate required inspections.
* Arrange utility coordination and power disconnection/reconnection as required.
* Complete the installation in accordance with applicable electrical codes and utility requirements.
* Test the completed electrical service and verify proper operation.

Long-Term Reliability and Protection

This comprehensive replacement addresses the deterioration affecting the existing overhead electrical service, including the improperly sealed meter base, moisture intrusion concerns, and signs of corrosion affecting the incoming service cable.

Replacing these components together allows LPH to address the existing points of concern while increasing the home’s electrical capacity from 100 Amps to 200 Amps.

The installation of protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections will also help preserve the service cable by reducing direct exposure to sunlight and physical damage. The new meter base and properly sealed connections will help reduce the potential for future moisture intrusion.

The new 200 Amp overhead service will provide:

* New 200 Amp meter base.
* New 200 Amp overhead service entrance cable.
* New service head and associated overhead service components.
* New 200 Amp exterior emergency disconnect.
* New 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* Whole-home surge protection.
* Complete grounding and bonding system.
* Increased electrical capacity for future home improvements.

This upgrade will give the homeowner a more reliable and modern electrical service while providing substantially more capacity for future electrical demands.

Peace-of-Mind Warranty

The new Eaton CH electrical panel and associated breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while the homeowner maintains an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, subject to applicable warranty terms.

LPH Recommendation

Based on the conditions identified during the electrical system evaluation, LPH recommends replacing the existing electrical service.

While a complete 100 Amp replacement would address the deteriorated equipment, LPH believes this is an excellent opportunity to consider upgrading to 200 Amps instead.

The majority of the work involved in replacing the existing service will already be necessary, regardless of whether the homeowner chooses to remain at 100 Amps or upgrade to 200 Amps. By increasing the service capacity now, the homeowner can avoid potentially having to replace the meter base, service entrance cable, emergency disconnect, and other associated equipment again if additional electrical capacity is needed in the future.

The additional capacity provides flexibility for future HVAC equipment, electric vehicle charging, appliance upgrades, home renovations, and other electrical improvements without having to start another complete service replacement project.

Our recommendation is to take advantage of the opportunity to upgrade the home’s electrical infrastructure now rather than simply replacing the existing equipment with the same 100 Amp capacity. This provides a more complete long-term investment, additional electrical capacity, and greater flexibility for the homeowner’s future needs.
e.440861946:
Grounding Electrode System & Bonding Upgrade

LPH will install a complete grounding and bonding system to help establish a proper path for electrical fault current and provide an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical system.

Scope of Work:

1. Install Two Grounding Electrodes
    * Install two new grounding rods at the exterior of the home, spaced and installed in accordance with applicable requirements.
    * Connect the grounding rods using appropriately sized grounding electrode conductor.
    * Ensure all connections are properly secured and protected.
2. Bond the Gas Piping
    * Install a properly sized bonding conductor to connect the home’s gas piping system to the electrical grounding and bonding system.
    * Secure the bonding connection with an approved grounding clamp.
    * This helps keep metal piping systems at the same electrical potential and provides a path for electrical fault current when applicable.
3. Properly Ground the Water Piping
    * Install the appropriate grounding connection to the home’s metal water piping system where required.
    * Connect the grounding conductor to the qualifying metal water piping using an approved grounding clamp.
    * Verify the connection is secure and properly integrated into the home’s grounding and bonding system.
4. Final Inspection & Verification
    * Inspect all newly installed grounding and bonding connections.
    * Verify conductors are properly secured and connections are complete.
    * Ensure the grounding and bonding installation meets applicable electrical requirements.

Why This Upgrade Is Important

The grounding and bonding system is an important part of the home’s overall electrical safety. It helps provide a low-impedance path for electrical fault current, allowing protective devices such as circuit breakers to operate when a qualifying fault occurs. Proper bonding also helps reduce unwanted voltage differences between metal piping systems and other grounded components.

LPH recommends completing this work to establish a more complete grounding and bonding system and help bring the home’s electrical infrastructure up to current applicable standards.

Performed heating system check on 4 zone oil boiler. The boiler also does the domestic water via a tankless coil. Please see attached evaluation form for system readings and photos. There were several concerns noted during today’s visit.

B. Pressure relief valve has been leaking when the boiler runs. It also opens at lower pressure than rated. 
C. Autofeed valve combo has leaked and is over pressurizing the boiler. 
D. Draft control on the smoke pipe is damaged and not functioning. I was able to keep it from free spinning but it is not properly regulating the exhaust draft
E. Primary control is original and take up to 2 minutes to shut off the burner when flame is not detected

We discussed options including fixing the immediate leaks, a larger piping project to address all near boiler piping leaks, cleaning the boiler, replacing the primary control, and replacing the boiler entirely. We will be returning Monday to handle the immediate leaking issues and boiler cleaning. Please see revised Option B for future consideration.

i.337165841:
During today’s electrical system check, LPH performed an evaluation of the home’s electrical system, including the electrical panel, breakers, internal connections, switches, receptacles, and accessible electrical devices throughout the home. We also evaluated the condition of the existing devices, checked for loose connections, signs of overheating, electrical arcing, physical damage, and general wear and deterioration. Exterior electrical devices and their protection against weather exposure and moisture intrusion were also reviewed.

During our inspection, LPH identified significant deterioration among the existing switches and receptacles. These devices are approximately 30 years old and have reached a point where multiple devices are showing signs of failure. We found cracked plastic housings, weakened connections, wiring slipping out of devices, and evidence of electrical arcing. Almost every electrical box we opened and inspected showed some degree of deterioration or connection concerns.

Before making any recommendations, we went over our findings directly with the homeowners and physically showed them the damaged devices and the conditions we discovered during the inspection. We explained how these devices deteriorate over time, why loose connections and electrical arcing are concerning, and the potential for overheating and electrical failure if these conditions are allowed to continue.

Recommendations & Options Reviewed With Homeowners:

1. Whole-Home Device Restoration: LPH recommended replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home. Since these devices were installed around the same time, the widespread deterioration indicates that similar issues can reasonably be expected in devices that have not yet been inspected or are not currently showing symptoms. Replacing everything together provides a comprehensive restoration rather than waiting for individual devices to fail. This option also includes a dimmer switch and two GFCI receptacles as an added value.
2. Partial Home Device Replacement: An alternative option was provided to replace up to 50 switches and receptacles, allowing the homeowners to prioritize the most deteriorated devices while addressing a significant portion of the identified concerns.
3. Exterior Device & Weatherproofing Upgrades: As part of the device replacement options, LPH also included upgrading applicable exterior receptacles to weather-resistant devices, installing two weather-resistant GFCI receptacles, adding exterior in-use bubble covers to protect receptacles from direct rain and moisture exposure, and sealing exterior electrical enclosures with silicone to help prevent water intrusion.

We explained the importance of addressing these conditions proactively, especially considering the age of the devices and the widespread deterioration already identified. Continuing to operate with damaged devices and compromised connections increases the potential for additional arcing, overheating, and electrical failures.

At this time, the homeowners will be sent the estimates along with today’s electrical system evaluation for their review and consideration. They can take the time to review the available options and determine how they would like to proceed.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure meeting with you, and we appreciate the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system.

e.438612387:
LPH recommends replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home. During today’s inspection, we found that the existing devices are approximately 30 years old and have deteriorated significantly from normal use and age. Multiple devices were found with cracked plastic housings, weakened wire connections, and wiring beginning to slip out of the devices. Evidence of electrical arcing was also identified.

After inspecting multiple locations throughout the home, it became apparent that these issues are not isolated to one or two devices. Nearly every electrical box inspected showed some degree of deterioration or connection concerns.

Because these devices were all installed around the same time, it is reasonable to expect similar wear throughout the remainder of the home, including locations that have not yet shown obvious symptoms. Continuing to operate with deteriorating devices increases the potential for electrical arcing, overheating, and eventual electrical failure.

LPH strongly recommends proactively replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home rather than addressing individual failures as they occur. This provides the homeowner with refreshed, secure electrical connections throughout the home and helps reduce the risk of future connection-related issues.

As an added value with this upgrade, LPH will include one dimmer switch and two GFCI receptacles at no additional charge.

Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

i.339355965:
LPH arrived at the home to perform a complete electrical system check and safety evaluation. During today’s inspection, we evaluated the electrical panel and breakers, wiring connections, grounding and bonding, safety devices, GFCI protection, switches, receptacles, and the overall condition of the electrical components throughout the home.

Findings and Recommendations:

* Exterior Receptacles: Several exterior receptacles were found to be rusted, along with existing gray outdoor covers that are not rated for locations exposed to direct rain. LPH recommends replacing these with weather-resistant (WR) outdoor receptacles and extra-duty, weatherproof in-use bubble covers rated for wet locations. These covers allow extension cords and other devices to remain plugged in while the protective cover stays fully closed and secured. All boxes will also be sealed with exterior-grade silicone around the edges to help prevent water from entering behind the covers and reaching the electrical connections.
* Arcing Light Switch: One single-pole switch was found to be actively arcing and was verified to have backstabbed wiring connections. These push-in connections can loosen or develop poor electrical contact over time, potentially leading to overheating and arcing. LPH recommends replacing this switch and securing the wiring under the proper screw terminals to provide a more reliable connection and reduce the potential for future electrical issues.
* Whole-Home Surge Protection: LPH also recommends installing a whole-home surge protector to provide an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical equipment and appliances. Everyday electrical activity from equipment such as air conditioners, refrigerators, furnaces, microwaves, and other appliances can create small electrical surges throughout the home’s wiring. Larger surges can also occur from utility disturbances or nearby lightning activity. These voltage spikes can gradually damage sensitive electronic components, circuit boards, televisions, computers, and modern appliances. Installing whole-home surge protection helps reduce the amount of damaging voltage that reaches these devices, providing added protection and peace of mind.

LPH reviewed all findings and available options with the homeowners so they could understand the recommended improvements and the benefits of addressing them. At this time, the homeowners are not interested in moving forward with any electrical maintenance or upgrades.

Today’s electrical system check evaluation and the estimates for the recommended improvements will be emailed to the homeowners for their records and future consideration.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure speaking with you, and we look forward to the opportunity to service you again in the future!

e.442752475:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

LPH returned today to complete the recommended electrical service replacement following the previous evaluation, which identified extensive water intrusion, corrosion, and moisture-related deterioration throughout the existing exterior meter base and interior electrical panel.

The existing water-affected service equipment was removed and replaced with a new electrical service assembly. This included installation of a new exterior meter base, emergency disconnect, conduit, and associated service wiring. New four-wire conductors were installed between the exterior disconnect and interior panel, allowing the interior panel to be properly reconfigured as a subpanel with the required separation of neutrals and grounds. The grounding and bonding systems were also addressed as part of the replacement, including the required bonding bridge and grounding connections.

All new grounding connections were established at the new exterior emergency disconnect. The existing grounding conductors were relocated from the interior panel to the new service disconnect, where the grounding system is now properly established. An additional grounding connection was also installed to the home’s metal water piping, providing the necessary supplementary grounding and bonding required by applicable electrical code.

A new 42-space Eaton CH electrical loadcenter was installed to replace the existing moisture-damaged panel. All existing branch-circuit wiring was properly relocated and terminated into the new panel. The entire panel was fully identified and relabeled to provide accurate circuit identification for the homeowners and for future electrical servicing.

Whole-home surge protection was also installed to provide an additional layer of protection against damaging voltage surges and electrical spikes that can affect appliances, electronics, and other sensitive equipment throughout the home.

As an additional measure to help prevent future water intrusion, the entire new service assembly was carefully sealed. All areas where electrical wiring, conduit, or other piping enter the home were fully sealed with silicone, along with the appropriate service entry points and exterior equipment connections. This helps close potential pathways for water to enter the home and protects the newly installed electrical equipment from exposure to outside moisture.

New weather-resistant exterior receptacles were also installed at both the front and back porches. The back porch receptacle was equipped with a new extra-duty in-use bubble cover to provide protection while the receptacle is being used and exposed to the elements. The existing cover at the front porch was inspected and remains code-compliant due to the protection provided by the porch overhang, so it was left in place.

Upon completion, all work was thoroughly inspected and tested. The new service equipment, panel, breakers, grounding and bonding connections, surge protection, and installed receptacles were tested and confirmed to be functioning properly. The electrical system was verified to be operating as intended before leaving.

Warranty Information: The newly installed service equipment is backed by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while the homeowners remain active members of the LPH Service Partner Plan.

i.339921329: This morning I arrived at the customers home to conduct their first annual electrical system check since their move in 2 months ago. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies, however I had one substantial estimate for the homeowners at the time of our check today. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main breaker panel. The panel appears to be in the end stages of progressive corrosion. I analyzed substantial rust on not only the panel housing but some segments of wiring as well. Most of the panels bare copper/ aluminum exhibit signs of oxidization or corrosion from moisture exposure over the span of 50+ years.  The panel has eclipsed what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is 50 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. We lose the ability to be able to gauge proper function of these breakers as they age until sometimes, we lose power entirely. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. Primarily the main breakers are the cause of concern. If the main breaker were to trip for any reason, there is a strong likelihood it would not reset, as it is not considered a “serviceable” breaker. The rest of the homes equipment appears to be in good condition with no other signs of potential failure. For all of the reasons listed above, I have provided a sole estimate today to replace the main breaker panel. Should you have any questions or concerns regarding todays visit or our findings, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you for having me out today and I look forward to our next visit!

i.340828630: This morning I arrived at the Bedford household to conduct the homes first annual electrical system and safety check. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service (Panel, Exterior Meterbase) I found several discrepancies. The primary concern related to today’s visit is the main load center itself. The home has a 55-60 year old Murray Electric Fuse Box. While not illegal per se, these fuse boxes can pose challenges for home sellers especially in a place like Manheim TWP. Should an inspection be performed, the inspector may require the seller to upgrade the existing service due to one its age, which has well exceeded what we would deem to be the average life expectancy of a panel (30-35 years) and two, potential fire hazards and recalls on these dated products. Historically Manheim is very concerned with maintaining a safe and up to date property. I have seen first hand sellers held to contingency and forced to make large, last minute updates or risk cancelling sales. As far as the physical conditon goes, the panel appears to be in OK shape, and I found no obvious signs of burning, melting, arcing, or major corrosion. however, with the age of the fuse box, there is no guarantee of its safety or its proper function. I informed Mrs. Bedford that in order to streamline the process of selling the home, and in order to receive better potential equity and general safety, it would be wise to upgrade the outdated system to a modern breaker panel set up. I have provided an estimate to upgrade the service at face value with a modern 100A counterpart, and then a more advanced upgrade to todays standard which is a 200A system. The primary goal is to achieve piece of mind, as well as ultimate safety in a customers home, whether it is the current owner or the next. Todays estimates are rooted in safety and upgrading all facets of the home as deemed necessary by the state for safe and comfortable homeownership. If you have any concerns related to todays visit, or any questions regarding the information I have provided you, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you for your time this afternoon and I look forward to our next visit!

We also checked the operation of the ceiling fan and its remote control system to identify any issues affecting normal operation.

* Electrical Panel: (2) existing 20-amp breakers were found to be noticeably loose and outdated. * Interior Receptacles: (3) duplex receptacles were identified for replacement. These conditions can lead to intermittent operation, poor electrical connections, and potential overheating.
* Kitchen GFCI: (1) kitchen GFCI receptacle had a physically deteriorating face with portions beginning to crack off. The homeowner also reported issues with the device tripping. Replacement was recommended to restore dependable operation and GFCI protection.
* Ceiling Fan: The existing ceiling fan remote receiver assembly required replacement to restore reliable communication between the remote and fan.

LPH reviewed the findings and recommendations with the homeowner, and all of the above-listed work was approved, completed, and tested today. The two 20-amp breakers, three duplex receptacles, kitchen GFCI receptacle, and ceiling fan remote receiver assembly were replaced.

All completed work was tested, and proper operation was verified prior to leaving the home.

Today’s electrical system check evaluation and invoice summary will be emailed to the homeowner for their records.

Thank you for choosing LPH and allowing us the opportunity to service your home. We appreciate your business!

Performed heating system check on gas boiler. Please see attached evaluation form for system readings. During the inspection we identified and reviewed with the customer the following concerns:

A. There is significant dust and rust accumulated on the burners and inside the fire chamber of the boiler. 
**Recommended a boiler cleaning**

B. There is an active leak on the pressure relief valve and a smaller one on one of the zone shutoff valves. The riser on the pressure relief valve is severely rusted from the leak. Autofill valve has been slowly adding water to accommodate. 
**Recommended replacing the pressure relief valve and riser, autofill valve, and zone shutoff valve**

C. The gas line around the boiler has several inappropriate fittings. Two outdated gas shutoffs are present and a thread protector is being used as a coupling. There is a heightened risk of gas leak from these fittings. 
**Recommended replacing those fittings**

We also recommended the customer replace the existing laundry room door with a louvered door to allow proper combustion air to reach the boiler and water heater. 

System is heating at this time.

e.440432415:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations. However, we identify that these existing units are past their 10 year life expiration. Lastly, we identified the washer circuit does not contain proper GFI protection and the front exterior GFI has sticking buttons which could indicate improper function. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. Water flow
