e.440546198:
LPH recommends installing a dedicated portable generator connection to allow the homeowner to safely power selected electrical circuits throughout the home during a power outage. This installation will provide a permanent, convenient connection point for the homeowner-supplied generator while incorporating the necessary electrical connections and safety equipment.

Scope of Work:

1. 50-Amp Generator Connection

* Run a new dedicated 50-amp, 120/240-volt electrical circuit from the existing electrical panel to a new exterior generator inlet box.
* Install the appropriately sized wiring and 50-amp double-pole breaker.
* Install a weather-rated exterior generator inlet box with a properly sized four-wire connection.
* Secure and protect wiring throughout the installation.

2. Electrical Panel Interlock Kit

* Install a manufacturer-approved interlock kit compatible with the existing electrical panel.
* Install the dedicated generator backfeed breaker and associated connections.
* The interlock provides a mechanical safety feature that prevents the utility main breaker and generator breaker from being turned on simultaneously.
* When operating on generator power, the utility main breaker must be turned OFF before the generator breaker can be engaged. This prevents generator power from feeding backward into utility lines, helping protect utility workers and preventing dangerous electrical backfeed.
* Properly label the electrical panel with generator operating instructions.

Important Information for the Homeowner:

* This installation allows the homeowner to use their portable generator to supply power to selected circuits throughout the home during a utility outage.
* The generator will not automatically turn on when utility power is lost. The homeowner will need to manually start the generator, connect the generator cord to the exterior inlet, and operate the panel interlock according to the provided instructions.
* The number of appliances and electrical circuits that can operate simultaneously will depend on the generator’s wattage and available capacity. Larger appliances, HVAC equipment, electric water heaters, and other high-demand equipment may require load management to prevent overloading the generator.
* The homeowner-supplied generator must be compatible with the 50-amp connection and the home’s electrical configuration. LPH will verify compatibility before completing the installation.
* The generator must always be operated outdoors, away from windows, doors, and other openings to prevent dangerous carbon monoxide from entering the home.
* The generator must be operated according to the manufacturer’s instructions, including proper grounding and neutral configuration requirements.

Installation & Verification:

All new electrical connections, generator inlet equipment, breakers, and interlock components will be installed and verified for proper operation. Applicable permits and inspections will be addressed as required.

This installation provides the homeowner with a safer, more convenient way to maintain essential power during unexpected outages without relying on extension cords running throughout the home.

LPH appreciates the opportunity to provide this estimate and help improve the home’s backup power capabilities.
e.440550127:
LPH recommends installing a dedicated portable generator connection to allow the homeowner to safely power selected electrical circuits throughout the home during a power outage. This installation will provide a convenient connection point for the homeowner-supplied generator while incorporating the necessary electrical and propane gas connections, whole-home surge protection, and safety equipment to ensure proper operation.

Scope of Work:

1. 50-Amp Generator Connection
    * Run a new dedicated 50-amp, 120/240-volt electrical circuit from the existing electrical panel to a new exterior generator inlet box.
    * Install the appropriate wiring, 50-amp double-pole breaker, and weather-rated generator connection box.
    * Provide a properly sized four-wire connection to accommodate the generator’s power output.
    * Secure and protect wiring throughout the installation.
2. Generator Propane Gas Line Installation
    * Install approximately 60 feet of 3/4-inch TracPipe propane gas piping from the existing propane hookup to the generator location.
    * Route the piping through the basement drop ceiling and continue to the designated exterior generator location.
    * Install the necessary fittings, connections, and shutoff provisions.
    * Verify the completed propane gas piping installation for proper operation and leaks.
    * Propane gas piping will need to be properly sized and verified for the generator’s BTU requirements and the existing propane system’s capacity.
3. Electrical Panel Interlock Kit
    * Install a manufacturer-approved interlock kit compatible with the existing electrical panel.
    * Install the dedicated generator backfeed breaker and associated connections.
    * The interlock provides a mechanical safety feature that prevents the utility main breaker and generator breaker from being turned on simultaneously.
    * When operating on generator power, the main utility breaker must be turned OFF before the generator breaker can be engaged. This prevents generator power from feeding backward into the utility lines, protecting utility workers and preventing an unsafe electrical backfeed condition.
    * Properly label the panel with generator operating instructions.
4. Whole-Home Surge Protection
    * Install a whole-home surge protection device at the electrical service or panel to help protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment.
    * The surge protection is intended to help protect against uneven voltage and transient voltage fluctuations that may occur as the generator starts up, cycles, or changes load.
    * Install and connect the surge protection equipment in accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements and applicable electrical codes.

Important Information for the Homeowner:

* This installation is designed to allow the homeowner to use their portable generator to supply power to selected circuits throughout the home during a utility outage.
* The generator will not automatically turn on when the utility power goes out. The homeowner will need to manually start the generator, connect the generator cord to the exterior inlet, and operate the panel interlock according to the provided instructions.
* The amount of equipment and appliances that can operate simultaneously will depend on the generator’s wattage and available capacity. Larger appliances, HVAC equipment, electric water heaters, and other high-demand equipment may require load management to prevent overloading the generator.
* The homeowner-supplied generator must be compatible with the 50-amp connection and the home’s electrical configuration. LPH will verify compatibility before completing the installation.
* The generator must always be operated outdoors, away from windows, doors, and other openings to prevent dangerous carbon monoxide from entering the home.
* The generator must be operated according to the manufacturer’s instructions, including proper grounding and neutral configuration requirements.
* The generator’s propane supply must be adequate for the generator’s required BTU input and operating duration. Propane tanks and fuel supply must be maintained in accordance with the generator manufacturer’s instructions and applicable codes.
* Whole-home surge protection helps reduce the risk of damage from voltage surges and fluctuations but does not guarantee protection from all electrical events or equipment damage.

Installation & Verification:

All new electrical connections, generator inlet equipment, interlock components, whole-home surge protection equipment, and propane gas piping will be installed and verified for proper operation. Applicable permits and inspections will be addressed as required.

This installation provides the homeowner with a safer, more convenient way to maintain essential power during unexpected outages without relying on extension cords running throughout the home.

LPH appreciates the opportunity to provide this estimate and help improve the home’s backup power capabilities.

i.438274464:
I was out today to discuss options for replacing the homeowners’ current HVAC system with a newer, more energy-efficient system.

During our conversation, the homeowners mentioned they are preparing to leave for Florida for the winter and will be away for approximately five months. While reviewing their existing heat pump, we discussed that the dual capacitor is nearing the limits of its operating specifications. I explained that if the capacitor fails, it could prevent the heat pump from starting and operating properly while they are away, potentially leaving the home without heat.

At this time, the homeowners are primarily interested in gathering pricing for a future system replacement. I reviewed the benefits of upgrading to a new system, including improved energy efficiency, all-new equipment, a 10-year parts warranty, and a 10-year labor warranty. We also discussed the benefits of a Wi-Fi thermostat, which would allow them to remotely monitor and control their HVAC system while they are in Florida, providing additional peace of mind.

After reviewing everything, the homeowners decided they would prefer to hold off on replacing the system for now and requested that all options be emailed over for their review.

I left my business card with my contact information and encouraged them to call or text me with any questions or concerns.

Thank you again for allowing me into your home today and giving me the opportunity to go over your HVAC replacement options. I look forward to working with you when the time is right.

Wishing you both safe travels, a wonderful winter in Florida, and I look forward to reconnecting in the spring!

Today I was called out to address several concerns at the home. The homeowner requested that all openings be sealed to help prevent critters from entering the property. She also reported experiencing intermittent power issues.

I inspected all electrical connections at the panel, meter base, and transfer switch. All connections appeared to be in good condition. However, I noticed the meter base is slowly pulling away from the wall due to ground settling. I recommended installing a slip riser to prevent future stress or damage to the meter base and service connections.

All voltage readings were within acceptable ranges.

The homeowner also reported that the pond pump had been tripping the breaker intermittently. I inspected the breaker and associated outlets but did not find any apparent issues. I advised the homeowner to unplug the pump during the next rain event to determine whether the issue is being caused by the pump itself or potentially damaged wiring along the circuit.

Due to the reported power issues, I also recommended installing whole-home surge protection to help protect the home’s electrical equipment and appliances from potential voltage surges. The homeowner declined the recommendation at this time due to cost and chose to hold off until next year.

All requested openings were sealed, and the invoice was emailed to the homeowner.

We also identified that the existing outlets in the home contained push in/backstab style connections, which can loosen up quicker overtime. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. Findings and Recommendations:

During today’s evaluation, we identified an opportunity to improve the circuit separation for the sump pump and water softener. Both appliances were currently spliced into the living room GFCI circuit through a junction box located beside the electrical panel. Sharing this circuit can contribute to nuisance GFCI tripping and potentially interrupt power to the sump pump and water softener when the living room circuit experiences an issue.

LPH went over the following recommendations with the homeowner:

* Dedicated Circuit Separation: Install a new 15-amp breaker and approximately 10 feet of new wiring to separate the sump pump and water softener from the living room GFCI circuit. The existing junction box beside the panel would be remade and properly re-spliced to separate the circuits and help eliminate nuisance GFCI tripping.
* Garage GFCI Protection: Install a new GFCI receptacle in the garage to provide additional protection against electrical shock.
* Whole-Home Surge Protection: Install a whole-home surge protection device at the electrical panel to help protect appliances, electronics, and sensitive equipment from damaging voltage spikes caused by utility fluctuations, lightning, and everyday operation of larger electrical equipment.

Completed Work:

The homeowner elected to move forward with the dedicated circuit separation. LPH installed the new 15-amp breaker, ran approximately 10 feet of new wiring, and remade the existing junction box beside the panel to properly separate the sump pump and water softener from the living room GFCI circuit.

e.438790197:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

i.438645175:
During today’s electrical system check, LPH performed an evaluation of the home’s electrical system, including the main electrical panel, breakers, visible wiring and connections, grounding and bonding, receptacles, switches, GFCI protection, exterior electrical devices, smoke detectors, and general electrical safety throughout the home. We also reviewed the overall condition and age of the existing electrical equipment and discussed potential improvements to the home’s electrical safety, reliability, and functionality.

GFCI Protection & Electrical Safety

We reviewed several areas throughout the home where GFCI protection is important, particularly the kitchen countertop receptacles, as well as other locations such as the washing machine receptacle and other areas where protection is required. GFCI devices are designed to quickly interrupt power when they detect an electrical current imbalance, helping reduce the risk of electrical shock, especially in areas where water and electricity may come into contact.

Exterior Receptacles & Weather Protection

We discussed the importance of having properly weather-rated electrical devices and enclosures at all exterior locations. One existing exterior GFCI located on the outside wall of the garage was found tripped, with evidence of water intrusion being a concern. The existing gray exterior cover is not properly rated for the exposed location and does not provide the necessary protection against direct weather exposure. Proper weather-resistant GFCI devices and appropriately rated in-use covers help protect electrical connections from rain and moisture, reducing the potential for corrosion, nuisance tripping, and premature device failure.

Back-Stabbed Electrical Devices

We also reviewed locations throughout the home where receptacles and switches were originally wired using the back-stab connection method. These connections rely on internal spring tension to hold the wiring in place rather than the more secure screw-terminal connections. Over time, these connections can lose their holding tension, potentially allowing wires to loosen. Loose connections can create electrical resistance, excessive heat, intermittent operation, and potentially electrical arcing or damage to the devices. We explained why upgrading these devices to properly secured connections can help improve long-term reliability and reduce the potential for overheating.

Smoke & Carbon Monoxide Detection

We discussed adding an additional smoke detector for the downstairs bedroom to provide appropriate detection and notification in that sleeping area. e.438882972:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

i.438814646:
Homeowner mentioned that there was no hot water coming out of the kitchen faucet. Technician removed the cover from the Noritz tankless water heater and connected a hose to the hot-water outlet service port to verify that the unit was firing and producing a flame at the heat exchanger. Technician cleaned the flame rod and igniter rod and noticed an improvement in the flame after cleaning. Technician then checked the hot-water temperature at the kitchen sink and recorded a temperature of 122°F, confirming that the unit was producing hot water.

Technician explained to the homeowner why it takes additional time for hot water to reach the kitchen sink. Technician also showed the homeowner the water distribution manifold and explained the hot-water piping layout and the path the water travels from the tankless water heater to the kitchen faucet.

Technician recommends scheduling routine maintenance on the Noritz tankless water heater. Routine maintenance includes flushing the heat exchanger to help remove mineral buildup, cleaning the flame rods, inspecting and cleaning the air intake screen, and cleaning the cold-water inlet filter. Regular maintenance helps maintain proper operation, improve efficiency, and extend the service life of the tankless water heater.

e.438849219: Technician performed routine maintenance on the tankless water heater. Technician flushed and descaled the heat exchanger to remove mineral buildup and help maintain optimal efficiency and performance. The flame rods were removed and cleaned to ensure proper flame sensing and reliable operation. Technician also cleaned the fresh air intake screen and cold water inlet screen to promote proper airflow and water flow through the unit. After maintenance was completed, the water heater was tested for proper operation. Unit was operating normally at the time of service and was left in good working condition.

i.438969112:
LPH arrived at the home to perform a comprehensive electrical system check evaluation. During our inspection, we found that the home’s electrical system is in a considerably deteriorated condition. Several major components, including the electrical service, main panel, branch-circuit wiring, receptacles and switches, and smoke detection devices, are aging or in need of improvements. We discussed with the homeowners that addressing these items over time would help bring the home closer to current electrical safety standards, improve overall system reliability, and provide a safer electrical environment for the property.

During today’s evaluation, we reviewed the following recommendations and provided separate estimates for the homeowners’ consideration:

1. Complete Electrical Service Replacement

Our first and most important recommendation is to replace the existing electrical service and associated equipment. This would provide a properly updated foundation for the home’s electrical system and help ensure the service can adequately accommodate the additional electrical improvements planned throughout the property. We recommend prioritizing this project before investing in the remaining electrical upgrades.

2. Non-Grounded Receptacle & GFCI Safety Upgrades

Replace the existing non-grounded receptacles throughout the home with GFCI-protected receptacles. Additionally, install GFCI protection at the kitchen, bathroom, and exterior receptacles. The exterior receptacle will also receive a new weather-resistant in-use bubble cover to provide better protection against moisture and outdoor exposure. These improvements will provide additional protection against electrical shock, particularly in areas where proper grounding is not currently available.

3. Basement Electrical Rewiring & Circuit Improvements

Rework the accessible basement wiring by installing new electrical runs for the dryer and sump pump. This includes approximately 10 feet of new wiring for each, with the dryer wiring protected in properly secured conduit along the basement wall and new receptacles installed for both appliances. We will also install a new grounded 12/2 Romex circuit in the mechanical room to improve the condition and reliability of the accessible basement electrical wiring.

Additional System Recommendations

Beyond the individual estimates provided, we discussed the importance of addressing the overall condition of the home’s electrical system. This includes evaluating and updating the aging electrical panel, deteriorated service components, existing branch-circuit wiring, receptacles and switches, and smoke detection throughout the property. Proper smoke detection is an essential part of the home’s overall electrical and fire safety, and outdated or insufficient devices should be brought up to current safety recommendations.

Moving Forward:

We understand that these improvements represent a considerable investment, and the homeowners would like some time to review the options, plan accordingly, and determine which projects they would like to move forward with first. Our professional recommendation is to begin with the complete electrical service replacement, as this will establish a more reliable and appropriate foundation to support the additional upgrades throughout the home.

The goal is to work toward improving the home’s overall electrical safety, reliability, and functionality while bringing the system closer to current standards. We appreciate the opportunity to evaluate the property and provide these recommendations so the homeowners can make informed decisions about their next steps.

Today’s electrical system evaluation and all estimates will be emailed to the homeowners for review and future consideration.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate your time and the opportunity to help improve the safety and reliability of your electrical system. We look forward to working with you in the future!

e.441573170:
Complete 100 Amp Overhead Electrical Service Replacement

Existing Electrical Service Concerns

During the electrical system evaluation, LPH identified significant deterioration affecting the home’s existing 100 Amp electrical service and interior panel.

The home currently has an older 100 Amp, 12-space electrical panel that has experienced water intrusion associated with the exterior service cable entering the home. Upon inspection, corrosion was visible on the interior portions of the service cable conductors. The exterior service equipment is also compromised and not properly sealed, allowing moisture to enter the electrical system.

Additionally, small tears and damage are visible in the exterior service cable insulation. These openings can allow moisture to reach the conductors and contribute to further corrosion and deterioration of electrical connections. Continued exposure to moisture and corrosion can increase electrical resistance, contribute to overheating, and compromise the long-term reliability of the service.

We also identified the need to update the home’s grounding and bonding system to provide the appropriate electrical fault-current path and bring the service equipment up to current applicable requirements.

Due to the condition of the existing panel, corrosion on the service conductors, compromised exterior service components, and outdated grounding system, LPH recommends a complete 100 Amp electrical service replacement rather than attempting to reuse deteriorated equipment.

Scope of Work Includes

1. New 100 Amp Overhead Electrical Service & Meter Base

* Remove the existing deteriorated meter base and associated exterior service components.
* Install a new properly rated 100 Amp meter base.
* Remove and replace the existing overhead service entrance cable with new properly sized service conductors.
* Install a new service head/weatherhead assembly.
* Replace associated overhead service components as needed.
* Properly secure and support the new overhead service cable.
* Properly seal the meter base and all applicable service entry points to help prevent future moisture intrusion.
* Install protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections to help protect against sunlight exposure and physical damage.
* Properly terminate, secure, and torque all service connections in accordance with manufacturer specifications and applicable electrical requirements.

2. New 100 Amp Exterior Emergency Disconnect

* Install a new 100 Amp exterior emergency service disconnect.
* Properly connect and configure the disconnect as part of the new electrical service.
* Install required identification and labeling.
* Verify proper operation as part of the completed installation.

The exterior emergency disconnect provides an accessible means of shutting off power to the home during an emergency or when electrical service work is required. This also provides an updated service configuration in accordance with applicable electrical requirements.

3. New Interior Electrical Panel – 30-Space Eaton CH

* Remove the existing older 100 Amp, 12-space electrical panel.
* Install a new 30-space Eaton CH electrical panel rated for the home’s 100 Amp service.
* Transfer and properly terminate existing branch circuit wiring where conductors are suitable for reuse.
* Inspect accessible branch circuit conductors and connections for signs of corrosion, water damage, overheating, or deterioration.
* Install appropriately sized breakers for the existing circuits.
* Properly configure neutral and grounding connections at the new service equipment.
* Properly label the new panel and identify the branch circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation.

The new 30-space Eaton CH panel will provide updated electrical equipment and additional breaker space compared to the existing 12-space panel. This will give the homeowner greater flexibility for organizing existing circuits and accommodating future electrical needs.

4. Whole-Home Surge Protection

* Install a premium whole-home surge protective device at the new electrical panel.
* Properly integrate the surge protection into the electrical system.
* Verify proper installation and operation.

Whole-home surge protection provides an additional layer of defense against damaging voltage spikes and transient surges that can affect appliances, electronics, and sensitive electrical equipment.

Surges can enter the home through the utility supply during lightning activity or utility disturbances. They can also originate inside the home when equipment such as air conditioners, refrigerators, washers, dryers, dishwashers, and other motor-driven appliances cycle on and off.

Installing surge protection helps reduce the risk of damage to sensitive electronics, HVAC control boards, appliance circuit boards, LED lighting components, and other connected equipment.

5. Complete Grounding & Bonding Upgrade

* Install two new exterior grounding rods.
* Connect the grounding electrodes using properly sized grounding electrode conductors.
* Run a new grounding conductor to the home’s qualifying metal water piping at the water meter.
* Install an approved grounding clamp and secure the water-piping grounding connection.
* Install the appropriate bonding conductor and approved clamp for the home’s metal gas piping.
* Properly configure grounding and bonding connections at the new electrical service equipment.
* Verify the completed grounding and bonding system.

A properly installed grounding and bonding system is an essential part of the home’s electrical safety. It helps provide a low-impedance path for electrical fault current so protective devices can operate as intended during qualifying electrical faults. Proper bonding also helps reduce unwanted voltage differences between metal piping systems and other grounded components throughout the home.

6. Permits, Inspections & Utility Coordination

* Coordinate with PPL for the required overhead electrical service replacement.
* Obtain applicable permits.
* Coordinate required electrical inspections.
* Arrange utility power disconnection and reconnection as required.
* Complete the installation in accordance with applicable electrical codes and utility requirements.
* Test the completed service, panel, and associated equipment to verify proper operation.

Long-Term Reliability & Protection

This complete service replacement addresses the deterioration affecting both the exterior and interior portions of the home’s electrical service.

The existing service has experienced moisture intrusion, corrosion on the incoming conductors, compromised exterior cable insulation, and deterioration of the existing meter base and service components. Replacing the equipment together allows LPH to address these concerns rather than continuing to rely on components that have already shown signs of moisture damage and corrosion.

The new installation will provide:

* New 100 Amp meter base.
* New overhead service entrance cable and service head/weatherhead.
* New exterior 100 Amp emergency disconnect.
* New 30-space Eaton CH electrical panel.
* New appropriately sized breakers.
* Whole-home surge protection.
* Two new grounding rods.
* Updated grounding connection to the water piping.
* Proper bonding of the gas piping.
* Updated grounding and bonding connections throughout the service equipment.

The new exterior service components will be properly secured and sealed to help reduce the potential for future moisture intrusion. Protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections will also help protect the new service conductors from sunlight exposure and physical damage.

The new 30-space panel will provide additional circuit capacity compared to the existing 12-space equipment, while the surge protection and updated grounding system will add important layers of protection for the home’s electrical equipment.

Peace-ofMind Warranty

The new Eaton CH electrical panel and associated breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while the homeowner maintains an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, subject to applicable warranty terms.

LPH Recommendation

Based on the conditions identified during the electrical system evaluation, LPH recommends a complete replacement of the home’s existing 100 Amp electrical service.

The existing panel and service equipment have experienced moisture intrusion and corrosion, and the exterior service cable insulation has visible damage. These are concerns that extend beyond the age of the equipment and make continued reliance on the existing service components less desirable.

Rather than replacing only the panel or addressing individual exterior components separately, completing the entire service replacement allows LPH to install new, properly coordinated equipment from the exterior service connection through the interior panel, along with updated grounding, bonding, and surge protection.

This investment will provide the homeowner with a more dependable electrical service, additional breaker space, improved protection against moisture-related deterioration, and a stronger foundation for the home’s future electrical needs while maintaining the existing 100 Amp service capacity.

e.441574715:
100 Amp Exterior Overhead Electrical Service Replacement

Existing Exterior Service Concerns

During the electrical system evaluation, LPH identified deterioration affecting the home’s existing 100 Amp overhead electrical service.

The existing meter base is compromised and not properly sealed, allowing moisture to enter the electrical enclosure. We also observed small tears and damage in the insulation of the overhead service cable. These openings can allow moisture to reach the conductors, contributing to corrosion and deterioration of the electrical connections.

Corrosion and moisture intrusion at service connections can increase electrical resistance, contribute to overheating, and affect the long-term reliability of the electrical service.

Due to the condition of the existing exterior equipment and visible damage to the service cable, LPH recommends replacing the exterior service components rather than continuing to rely on deteriorated equipment.

Scope of Work Includes

1. New 100 Amp Meter Base

* Remove the existing compromised meter base.
* Install a new properly rated 100 Amp meter base.
* Properly mount and secure the new equipment.
* Seal the meter base and applicable entry points to help prevent future moisture intrusion.
* Properly terminate and secure all service connections according to manufacturer specifications.

2. New Overhead Service Entrance Cable

* Remove the existing damaged overhead service cable.
* Install new properly sized 100 Amp overhead service conductors.
* Install a new service head/weatherhead assembly.
* Replace associated exterior overhead service components as required.
* Properly secure and support the new overhead service cable.
* Install protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections to help protect against sunlight exposure and physical damage.
* Properly terminate and secure all connections.

Replacing the existing cable will eliminate the need to continue relying on insulation that has visible tears and damage and help reduce the potential for future moisture-related deterioration.

3. New 100 Amp Exterior Emergency Disconnect

* Install a new 100 Amp exterior emergency service disconnect.
* Properly connect and configure the disconnect as part of the exterior service replacement.
* Install required identification and labeling.
* Verify proper installation and operation.

The exterior emergency disconnect provides an accessible means of shutting off electrical power to the home during an emergency or when electrical service work is required.

4. Permits, Inspections & Utility Coordination

* Coordinate with PPL for the required exterior overhead service replacement.
* Obtain applicable permits.
* Coordinate required inspections.
* Arrange utility power disconnection and reconnection as required.
* Complete the installation in accordance with applicable electrical codes and utility requirements.
* Test the new exterior service equipment and verify proper operation.

Long-Term Reliability & Protection

This estimate focuses on replacing the deteriorated exterior components responsible for supplying electrical power to the home.

The new installation will provide:

* New 100 Amp meter base.
* New 100 Amp overhead service entrance cable.
* New service head/weatherhead.
* Properly secured and supported overhead service components.
* Properly sealed meter base and service entries.
* Protective conduit over applicable exterior cable sections.
* New 100 Amp exterior emergency disconnect.

Replacing these components together allows LPH to address the compromised meter base, damaged service cable insulation, and moisture intrusion concerns while providing updated exterior service equipment.

Important Scope Clarification

This estimate is strictly for the exterior 100 Amp overhead electrical service replacement.

The existing interior electrical panel will remain in place. This estimate does not include:

* Replacement of the existing interior 12-space electrical panel.
* Replacement of interior branch circuit breakers.
* Interior branch-circuit wiring repairs or modifications.
* Installation of whole-home surge protection.
* Installation or replacement of the grounding electrode system.
* Grounding or bonding upgrades to the water or gas piping.

These items can be addressed separately through additional estimates if the homeowner chooses to move forward with them.

LPH Recommendation

Based on the visible deterioration and damage affecting the existing exterior service equipment, LPH recommends replacing the exterior 100 Amp service components.

Although replacing only the exterior service will not address the water intrusion and corrosion already identified at the interior panel and cable connections, it will replace the compromised exterior equipment and provide a new meter base, service cable, and emergency disconnect.

This option allows the homeowner to address the exterior service concerns while keeping the existing interior panel and other electrical improvements separate for future consideration.

i.439010033:
LPH arrived at the home to perform an electrical system check evaluation. During today’s visit, we inspected the accessible electrical components and discussed several recommendations with the homeowner to improve the safety, reliability, and overall protection of the home’s electrical system.

During the evaluation, LPH identified the following areas for improvement:

1. GFCI Protection Upgrades

LPH recommended installing (2) new GFCI receptacles to provide additional protection in areas where electricity and moisture may come into contact.

* Install (1) GFCI receptacle at the washing machine location.
* Install (1) GFCI receptacle at the kitchen countertop.
* Verify proper wiring and test both devices for correct operation.

GFCI protection helps reduce the risk of electrical shock by detecting unintended electrical current and quickly shutting off power when a ground fault is detected. These locations benefit from having this additional layer of protection.

2. Main Service Connection Maintenance

LPH recommended servicing the main electrical service connections at the meter base.

* Pull the electrical meter to safely access the main service cable connections at the lugs.
* Inspect accessible conductor connection points.
* Apply antioxidant compound to the accessible bare conductor connections.
* Reinstall the meter and restore power.
* Verify proper operation of the electrical service.

This maintenance is intended to help minimize oxidation and corrosion at accessible electrical connections, supporting reliable electrical contact and long-term service performance.

3. Supplementary Water Piping Grounding & Bonding

During the evaluation, LPH identified that the home transitions to plastic piping throughout the interior but does not have the incoming copper water piping from outside bonded to the electrical grounding system.

LPH recommended installing the appropriate bonding connection to the incoming metallic water piping where it enters the home.

This connection is important because even though the interior plumbing transitions to plastic, the incoming copper water piping remains a metallic component that must be properly considered as part of the home’s grounding and bonding system. Establishing this connection helps maintain proper electrical bonding and reduces the potential for unwanted electrical voltage on metallic piping.

4. Exterior Weather-Rated Receptacle Upgrades

LPH identified exterior receptacles that have experienced water penetration and corrosion due to exposure to direct rain.

LPH recommended replacing the affected devices with:

* New weather-resistant (WR) exterior receptacles.
* Extra-duty weatherproof in-use bubble covers.
* Proper sealing and protection of the exterior electrical boxes.

The upgraded covers are designed to remain closed while a cord is plugged into the receptacle, maintaining protection against rain and moisture during outdoor use.

These improvements will help prevent continued moisture intrusion, reduce corrosion-related deterioration, and restore dependable outdoor electrical functionality.

5. Repair Punctured Wiring & Install New TV Receptacle

LPH identified damaged electrical wiring associated with a punctured wire. To address this concern, LPH recommended installing a new receptacle behind the wall-mounted television and running a new section of wiring down to the existing receptacle directly below.

The proposed work includes:

* Install a new electrical box and receptacle behind the wall-mounted television.
* Run new electrical wiring down to the existing receptacle location.
* Properly terminate and secure all wiring connections.
* Address the compromised wiring as part of the repair.
* Test the new receptacle and verify proper circuit operation.

This provides a permanent electrical connection for the television while addressing the damaged wiring and eliminating the need for exposed extension cords.

6. Whole-Home Surge Protection

LPH recommended installing a whole-home surge protector to provide an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical equipment and connected devices.

Surges can enter the home from outside through the utility electrical service, including lightning activity, utility switching, and electrical disturbances on the power lines.

Surges can also originate inside the home when larger appliances and equipment cycle on and off. Common examples include air conditioning systems, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, washers, dryers, microwaves, and dishwashers.

These electrical fluctuations can gradually damage sensitive electronic components, circuit boards, LED lighting drivers, and other household equipment.

A whole-home surge protector helps manage these voltage spikes before they travel throughout the home’s electrical system, providing protection for multiple circuits and connected appliances.

Approved Work & Scheduling

After reviewing the evaluation and discussing the available options, the homeowner approved the following work:

* Installation of whole-home surge protection.
* Repair of the punctured electrical wiring and installation of the new receptacle behind the wall-mounted television.

LPH will coordinate the approved work and ensure all installations and repairs are properly tested and verified upon completion.

The homeowner would also like to receive the remaining estimates for the GFCI upgrades, main service connection maintenance, supplementary water piping grounding and bonding, and exterior weather-rated receptacle replacements for future consideration.

Today’s electrical system check evaluation and all estimates have been sent to the homeowner through email for review. LPH will call to schedule with her tomorrow.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. We appreciate the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system and provide recommendations to help keep your home safe, protected, and operating reliably. We look forward to assisting you with the remaining improvements in the future!

Although the home transitions to plastic piping throughout the interior, the incoming copper water service entering from outside still requires consideration as part of the home’s grounding and bonding system.

* Identify the incoming copper water piping where it enters the home.
* Install the appropriate grounding/bonding connection to the incoming metallic water piping.
* Bond the water piping to the home’s electrical grounding system.
* Verify the connection is secure and properly installed.

This connection provides an additional bonding path for the incoming metallic water piping, helping ensure it remains at the same electrical potential as the home’s grounding system. Even when the interior plumbing transitions to plastic, the incoming copper water piping should not be overlooked when evaluating the home’s grounding and bonding.

Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

With this option, we would complete a full removal of the existing HVAC equipment and ductwork in the attic and install a new, updated system.

The scope of work would include installing additional plywood to create a safe and accessible walking path throughout the attic. We would also install a new secondary drain pan, new condensate safety switches, and a new condensate drain line to provide added protection against potential water damage.

Additionally, we would rebuild both the return and supply trunk lines and install all new flexible ductwork connecting to the existing supply vents to ensure proper airflow and system performance.

This option would also include a new indoor air handler, outdoor condenser unit, and refrigerant line set. The new line set would be enclosed in SlimDuct for a clean, professional appearance on the exterior of the home.

The entire installation is expected to take approximately 1½ days to complete.

If you have any questions or concerns regarding this option or the installation process, please don’t hesitate to call or text me. Thank you again for the opportunity, and I look forward to working with you on this project.

i.439213359: This afternoon I arrived at the Mihoci family home to analyze a refrigerator fault. Upon my arrival I found that upon opening the refrigerator doors the GFCI for the fridge would trip. I noted that the breaker for the panel appears to be in good condition and is allowing a proper 122 volts to be sent to the refrigerator outlet. After actuating the doors a couple of times I was able to deduce that the GFCI only appears to trip when the left door, the one with the flapper (articulating mullion) is opened. I was able to slowly open the door and it did not trip the GFCI. With both doors open, I manually actuated the mullion and it immediately tripped the GFCI receptacle. The flapper (mullion) has a small heating element within it, as well as several sets of communication wires connected to the other fridge components such as the sensor on the top that activates the light and the sensor which tells the fridge that the door is closed. I figure that since the GFCI only appears to trip when it is actuated, that there is probably a damaged or kinked wire in its hinges that is short circuiting when it is opened or closed. Otherwise there could be moisture within this portion of the appliance causing the trip. I encouraged Mr. Mihoci to contact an appliance repair shop such as Brubaker inc. on Harrisburg Pike, and or Sears Home Services. If you require any further electrical services, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you for having me out this afternoon and I look forward to our next visit!

i.439226062:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, most of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, there are a few recommendations we assessed during this inspection. 

First we discovered that this electrical system is currently past the “end of life” range, which means the longevity is in question. This main electrical/distribution panel is also maxed out and most newer circuit or electrical equipment could not be installed within this existing panel. Lastly, there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water meter does not meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. Lastly, we identified an area with missing GFI protection, the exterior outlet on the detached garage. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. The basic electrical package was approved by the homeowner and completed today. We installed a brand new GFCI receptacle with an outdoor rated cover to properly protect the exterior receptacle on the detached garage. One year worry free parts and labor warranty will be included for this install. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

LPH responded to the home to investigate a reported hot, burning electrical smell coming from the basement. Upon arrival, we noticed a faint electrical burning odor as soon as we began descending the basement steps. We began a thorough investigation of the home’s electrical system, inspecting accessible junction boxes, electrical equipment, and appliances in an effort to identify the source of the smell.

During our investigation, we noticed a slight burnt motor odor coming from the dishwasher control panel. We also identified a much stronger burnt motor smell coming from the basement dehumidifier. Although the dehumidifier had reportedly not been operating for several days, turning the unit on caused the odor to become significantly stronger. The motor was visibly struggling, shuddering during operation, and producing several popping sounds. Based on these observations, the dehumidifier appears to have an internal motor or mechanical failure and should be replaced. Continued operation is not recommended.

Electrical Panel Findings:

When focusing our inspection on the home’s electrical panel, we immediately identified concerning evidence of previous water intrusion throughout the panel and multiple breakers. Visible conditions included:

* Rust buildup and corrosion around breaker screws, rivets, and other metal components.
* Dried water stains and mineral deposits that appeared to have pooled on top of breakers and traveled down their sides.
* Evidence of previous water accumulation along the bottom of the electrical panel.
* Corrosion and deterioration affecting multiple breaker components.
* Unusually rough connections when reinstalling several breakers onto the panel’s bus bar, suggesting that the breaker connection points may have been compromised by moisture and corrosion.

Although the bus bar itself did not show extensive visible corrosion, the condition of the affected breakers and their connection points is concerning. Corrosion and oxidation at electrical connection points can increase electrical resistance, creating unwanted heat buildup and potentially contributing to arcing or unreliable electrical connections.

We also noticed a slight internal overheating odor coming from some of the breakers during our inspection. While these findings are concerning and could potentially contribute to excessive heat within the electrical system, we cannot definitively identify the electrical panel as the source of the original burning smell reported in the basement.

LPH Recommendations:

Due to the visible water damage, corrosion, compromised breaker components, and questionable breaker-to-bus connections, LPH recommends addressing the electrical panel rather than continuing to operate it in its current condition.

We provided two options for the homeowner to review:

Option 1 – Complete Electrical Panel Replacement:
Replace the existing electrical panel with a new panel, including the necessary components and updates to bring the installation up to current applicable electrical code requirements. This option addresses the condition of the existing panel as a whole rather than simply replacing individual components that have already experienced water damage.

Option 2 – Complete Breaker Replacement:
Replace all existing breakers within the electrical panel due to the visible corrosion, water damage, and concerns surrounding their connection points. This option addresses the compromised breakers while retaining the existing panel and bus assembly. However, it does not eliminate the potential concerns associated with the existing panel itself.

Given the amount of water intrusion and deterioration observed, LPH’s professional recommendation is to proceed with the complete panel replacement. This provides the most comprehensive solution by replacing the affected electrical components and restoring dependable connections throughout the panel.

The homeowner was made aware of our findings and the two available options. We will provide the estimates along with today’s evaluation for review and consideration.

e.439555671:
Electrical Panel Replacement and Whole-Home Surge Protection

LPH recommends replacing the existing approximately 44- to 45-year-old electrical panel with a new premium 42-space Eaton CH electrical panel and installing whole-home surge protection.

The existing panel has been in service for several decades and is well beyond the typical service life of the equipment. As electrical components age, internal connections, bus bars, breakers, and terminations can deteriorate over time. This can increase the potential for overheating, poor electrical connections, nuisance breaker issues, and reduced reliability of the home’s electrical system.

Scope of Work Includes:

* Remove the existing electrical panel.
* Install a new premium 42-space Eaton CH load center.
* Transfer and properly terminate existing branch circuit wiring.
* Replace existing breakers with new, appropriately sized Eaton CH breakers.
* Install premium whole-home surge protection at the new electrical panel.
* Properly integrate and configure the surge protective device.
* Inspect accessible wiring and connections for signs of heat damage or deterioration.
* Properly label the new electrical panel and identify all branch circuits.
* Test the completed installation and verify proper operation.

Benefits of the Upgrade

The new 42-space Eaton CH panel will provide modern electrical distribution equipment with additional breaker capacity for the home’s existing and future electrical needs. This upgrade will improve electrical system organization, provide dependable circuit protection, and make future electrical maintenance and additions easier.

The whole-home surge protective device will help protect sensitive electronics, appliances, HVAC equipment, and other connected devices against damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and everyday electrical events.

Peace-of-Mind Warranty

Your new Eaton CH electrical panel and associated breakers are protected by a 10-year parts and labor warranty while maintaining an active LPH Service Partner Plan (SPP) membership, subject to applicable warranty terms.

LPH Recommendation

Replacing the aging electrical panel and installing whole-home surge protection provides an important improvement to the home’s electrical infrastructure. Rather than continuing to rely on decades-old electrical equipment, this upgrade provides modern distribution equipment, additional circuit capacity, and added protection for the home’s electrical investments.

LPH recommends completing this upgrade to improve the overall reliability, safety, and long-term performance of the home’s electrical system.

LPH will replace the existing underground service connections and associated conduit components as required to establish a properly protected and reliable electrical service. All underground service conductors will be installed in appropriate protective conduit, with properly secured connections and sealed entry points to help prevent moisture intrusion and protect the electrical service from environmental deterioration.

This installation helps protect the underground service conductors against physical damage, moisture exposure, and premature deterioration, providing a more dependable electrical connection for the home.

Interior Electrical Panel Replacement and Surge Protection

LPH will remove the existing approximately 44- to 45-year-old electrical panel and replace it with a new premium 42-space Eaton CH load center. As electrical equipment ages, internal components, bus connections, breakers, and terminations can deteriorate over time. This can increase the potential for overheating, poor electrical connections, nuisance breaker issues, and reduced reliability.

The new Eaton CH panel will provide modern electrical distribution equipment with additional breaker capacity for the home’s existing and future electrical needs. All existing branch circuits will be transferred and properly terminated with appropriately sized new breakers.

As part of this upgrade, LPH will install premium whole-home surge protection directly at the new electrical panel. This device helps protect sensitive electronics, appliances, and other connected equipment against damaging voltage surges caused by lightning, utility disturbances, and other electrical events.

LPH will install or upgrade the home’s grounding electrode system as required, including two grounding electrodes where required, properly sized grounding conductors, and bonding of applicable metal water piping and other qualifying metal systems.

An effective grounding and bonding system is an essential part of electrical safety. It provides a proper path for fault current and helps ensure protective devices operate as intended during an electrical fault.

i.439482025:
LPH arrived at the home to perform a comprehensive electrical system check evaluation. During our visit, we inspected the main electrical panel, breaker connections, accessible wiring, receptacles, switches, GFCI protection, exterior electrical equipment, and general electrical safety throughout the home.

During our evaluation, we found that the electrical panel is approximately 40 years old. Although it appears to be in good condition visually, electrical panels are generally rated for a service life of approximately 25–40 years. Additionally, this is a Challenger panel, a discontinued product line that has been known to develop loose breaker-to-bus-bar connections as the equipment ages.

While individually checking the breakers to verify proper contact, we identified two breakers that produced a slight sizzling sound, indicating possible arcing at their connections. After the initial arcing, both breakers appeared to settle down and the noise stopped. However, this does not necessarily mean the underlying issue has resolved, and there is a possibility that the arcing could return intermittently. Loose or deteriorating connections can create excessive resistance and heat buildup, potentially leading to further damage or overheating within the panel.

We recommend replacing the two breakers that demonstrated these conditions, one 15-amp and one 20-amp breaker. We also discussed the importance of beginning to plan for an eventual panel replacement due to the age of the equipment and the conditions identified during our inspection.

Additional Recommendations:

Front Exterior Receptacle & Weatherproofing: The front exterior receptacle is beginning to deteriorate, with visible cracking and weathered contact points. Although the existing receptacle is GFCI protected from inside the home, the receptacle itself is not weather-resistant, and the existing cover is not properly rated for direct rain exposure. We recommend installing a new weather-resistant receptacle and extra-duty in-use bubble cover, along with resealing the exterior box to help prevent moisture intrusion. As an added precaution, we will also seal around the exterior meter base enclosure, including the mounting openings and rear service cable connector, to help prevent water from entering behind the enclosure and potentially traveling into the electrical service equipment.

Basement Bathroom Washing Machine GFCI: We recommend installing a dedicated GFCI-protected receptacle for the washing machine located in the basement bathroom. This will provide additional protection against electrical shock in an area where water and moisture are present. GFCI protection is designed to quickly interrupt power when an electrical imbalance is detected, helping reduce the risk of shock.

Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection: We also recommend installing a premium whole-home surge protection device at the main electrical panel. Many homeowners associate power surges with lightning strikes, but a large percentage of everyday voltage fluctuations originate inside the home. Appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, microwaves, washers, dryers, and other equipment can generate smaller electrical surges as they cycle on and off. Over time, these fluctuations can place additional stress on sensitive electronics, circuit boards, appliances, and LED lighting. Installing whole-home surge protection provides an additional layer of defense by helping protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes before they travel throughout the home’s wiring.

We reviewed these findings and recommendations with the homeowner and discussed the importance of addressing the identified concerns to improve the home’s overall electrical safety, reliability, and protection. The estimates for the recommended improvements, along with today’s electrical system check evaluation, will be emailed to the homeowner for review and future consideration.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure speaking with you, and we look forward to the opportunity to service you again in the future!

e.441674215:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

A pressure reducing valve (PRV) is a plumbing device that automatically lowers the water pressure coming into a home or building from the municipal water supply and keeps it at a safe, consistent level.

Why would someone install one?
There are several important reasons:
Protect plumbing pipes: Excessive water pressure puts unnecessary stress on pipes, joints, and fittings.
Prevent leaks: High pressure can contribute to leaking connections and premature plumbing failures.
Protect appliances: Water heaters, washing machines, dishwashers, refrigerators, and other fixtures can be damaged by excessive pressure.
Extend fixture lifespan: Faucets, toilets, shower valves, and other plumbing components last longer when pressure is controlled.
Reduce water waste: Excessive pressure can cause faucets and showerheads to use more water than necessary.
Reduce water hammer: Lowering excessive pressure can help reduce banging noises in plumbing, although water hammer may require a separate solution.
